samasa.explanation: dūrā 'far, remote' is the head; duṣṭa 'the wicked' stands to it in the ablative: 'far from the wicked'. The genitive (duṣṭānām dūrā, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) gives the same sense, since words for 'far' take either case. The two members are simply juxtaposed.

components.note: √duṣ 'to be spoiled, to sin', past participle

names.meaning: She who is far from the wicked
names.significance: Traditionally: those who harm others cannot reach Her by worship alone, because their own malice keeps them away; the distance is theirs, not Hers.

meaning_check.note: 'Unapproachable by sinners' turned the ablative relation round; the name says She is far from the wicked (duṣṭa, not specifically 'sinners').

sandhi.rule: visarga sandhi: the final s of the prefix dus (dur) becomes r before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ, the r then kept before a vowel)

samasa.vigraha: दुष्टः आचारः दुराचारः; दुराचारस्य शमनी दुराचारशमनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: duṣṭaḥ ācāraḥ durācāraḥ; durācārasya śamanī durācāraśamanī
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: dur-ācāra 'evil conduct', a prādi compound in which the prefix dus 'bad, ill' qualifies ācāra 'conduct'. Outer layer: śamanī 'she who quells' is the head and takes the inner compound in the genitive: 'the quencher of evil conduct'. Durācāra may also denote the evil-doers themselves; the sense is the same.

components.note: appears as dur- before a vowel

components.meaning: she who quells, pacifies, puts an end to
components.note: √śam 'to be calm', causative, with the agent suffix -ana and feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who quells evil conduct
names.significance: Traditionally She both checks the wrongdoing of the world and, for the devotee, calms the inner tendencies that lead to wrong action.

meaning_check.note: ācāra is conduct, not 'customs'; śamanī is 'quelling, calming' rather than merely 'stopping'.

names.previous_split_issues: durācāra was given as one row; it is the prefix dus (dur) + ācāra 'conduct'.

samasa.explanation: The past participle varjitā 'free from, devoid of' is the head and the faults stand to it in the instrumental: 'devoid of faults'. The members are juxtaposed without sound change.

names.meaning: She who is free from all faults
names.significance: Traditionally the faults are those of embodied existence — attachment, aversion, delusion and the like — which cannot touch Her, as the sky is untouched by the clouds that pass through it.

samasa.explanation: -jña 'knowing' is a verbal noun from √jñā formed with the suffix ka (Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ), which only occurs with a preceding word (upapada); sarva 'all' is its object. The feminine is -jñā. No sound change at the junction.

names.meaning: She who is omniscient
names.significance: Her knowledge is not acquired piece by piece; She knows all because all is Her own self-awareness. Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.1.9 calls the Absolute 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit'.
names.previous_split_issues: jñā was glossed 'omniscient'; the member only means 'knowing', and omniscience comes from the compound.

samasa.explanation: sāndra 'dense, thick, abundant' qualifies karuṇā 'compassion', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose compassion is dense'. A karmadhāraya reading ('She who is dense compassion itself') is also possible. The members are juxtaposed.

names.meaning: She who shows intense compassion
names.significance: Traditionally Her compassion is 'dense' because it is unmixed: it does not wait to be earned.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: समानः च अधिकः च समानाधिकौ; समानाधिकाभ्याम् वर्जिता समानाधिकवर्जिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: samānaḥ ca adhikaḥ ca samānādhikau; samānādhikābhyām varjitā samānādhikavarjitā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: samāna 'equal' and adhika 'greater, superior' are joined as a dvandva, 'an equal and a superior'. Outer layer: the participle varjitā 'devoid of' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental: 'devoid of an equal or a superior'.

names.meaning: She who has neither equal nor superior
names.significance: The name echoes the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (6.8): 'na tat-samaś cābhyadhikaś ca dṛśyate' — none is seen equal to It, nor greater.
names.previous_split_issues: samānādhika was left as one row; it is the dvandva samāna 'equal' + adhika 'superior'.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya, followed by the taddhita suffix -maya (mayaṭ)
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: sarva-śakti 'all powers' (karmadhāraya, sarva qualifying śakti). To this the suffix -maya 'consisting of, made of' (mayaṭ, Pāṇini 5.4.21 in the sense of 'consisting abundantly of') is added, feminine -mayī: 'consisting of all powers'. The second step is a derivation, not a further compound; its gloss sarvaśaktisvarūpā shows the sense.

components.meaning: power, energy; also a goddess as a power

names.meaning: She who consists of all powers
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā every power — of will, knowledge and action, and every deity of the Śrīcakra's enclosures — is a portion of Her; She does not merely possess the powers, She is made of them.

meaning_check.note: -mayī means 'consisting of', so She is made of all powers rather than 'having' them; 'omnipotent' is an interpretation and was dropped.

names.previous_split_issues: mayī was glossed 'consisting of' correctly; the table missed that -maya is a suffix, not a compound member.

samasa.explanation: 'She to whom all auspicious things belong', i.e. from whom they come; maṅgala takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi. A karmadhāraya reading (sarvā cāsau maṅgalā ca, 'She who is wholly auspicious') is also current. The members are juxtaposed.

names.meaning: She who is the source of all that is auspicious
names.significance: The Devī Māhātmya salutes Her as 'sarvamaṅgala-māṅgalye', the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious.
names.previous_split_issues: maṅgalā was glossed 'auspiciousness'; maṅgalā is the feminine of the compound, not the abstract noun.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

samasa.vigraha: सती गतिः सद्गतिः; सद्गतिम् प्रददाति इति सद्गतिप्रदा
samasa.vigraha_iast: satī gatiḥ sadgatiḥ; sadgatim pradadāti iti sadgatipradā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: sat 'true, good' qualifies gati 'way, goal, destination' (karmadhāraya; the feminine satī takes the masculine stem sat, puṃvadbhāva). Outer layer: -pradā 'giving' (pra + √dā with the suffix -a) is the head and governs the inner compound as its object.

components.note: present participle of √as 'to be'; appears as sad- by jaśtva

names.meaning: She who bestows the true goal
names.significance: Sadgati is both the good path and its end, liberation; traditionally She grants each seeker the right way and, at last, the highest state.

meaning_check.note: pradā is 'giving', not 'leading'; sadgati is the true goal (ultimately liberation) as well as the right path.

names.previous_split_issues: 'sad' was given in its sandhi form; the stem is sat.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.explanation: īśvarī 'sovereign, ruling lady' is the head and sarva 'all' stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of all'.

names.meaning: She who is the sovereign of all
names.significance: Her rule extends over all that moves and does not move; nothing lies outside Her governance.

meaning_check.note: 'the living and non-living things' is commentary, not in the name; moved to significance.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is sarva + īśvarī, joined by guṇa.

names.meaning: She who is everything
names.significance: Traditionally: since She consists of all, there is nothing outside Her to pervade; the world is not a container She fills but Her own form.

meaning_check.note: -mayī means 'consisting of'; the name says She is made of everything, not that She 'pervades' it.

names.previous_split_issues: -mayī is a suffix, not an independent compound member (correctly glossed).

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya), followed by the possessive suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: सर्वे मन्त्राः सर्वमन्त्राः; सर्वमन्त्राणाम् स्वरूपम् सर्वमन्त्रस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति सर्वमन्त्रस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarve mantrāḥ sarvamantrāḥ; sarvamantrāṇām svarūpam sarvamantrasvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti sarvamantrasvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-mantra 'all mantras' (karmadhāraya). (2) sarvamantra-svarūpa 'the essential form of all mantras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; svarūpa is the head). (3) The possessive suffix -in (feminine -inī) makes the whole an adjective: 'She who has the essential form of all mantras', i.e. who is their very nature. Juxtaposition throughout.

components.meaning: whose own form is, having the nature of
components.note: sva 'own' + rūpa 'form', with the possessive suffix -in, feminine

names.meaning: She who is the essence of all the mantras
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā every mantra is a sound-form of the Goddess, and Her own fifteen-syllabled vidyā is held to contain them all.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वाणि यन्त्राणि सर्वयन्त्राणि; सर्वयन्त्राणि आत्मा यस्याः सा सर्वयन्त्रात्मिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvāṇi yantrāṇi sarvayantrāṇi; sarvayantrāṇi ātmā yasyāḥ sā sarvayantrātmikā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: sarva-yantra 'all yantras' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi with ātman 'self, nature' as final member, which takes the suffix -ka; the feminine is -ātmikā (a → i before the suffix, Pāṇini 7.3.44): 'She whose very self is all yantras', i.e. who is their nature.

components.meaning: having as its self or nature

names.meaning: She whose very nature is all the yantras
names.significance: Every yantra is a diagram of Her presence, and the Śrīcakra, king of yantras, contains them all.

meaning_check.note: -ātmikā means 'whose nature is'; 'the soul of' reversed the relation slightly.

names.previous_split_issues: yantrātmikā was left fused and glossed 'essence of all yantras'; it is yantra + ātmikā.

samasa.vigraha: सर्वाणि तन्त्राणि सर्वतन्त्राणि; सर्वतन्त्राणि रूपम् यस्याः सा सर्वतन्त्ररूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvāṇi tantrāṇi sarvatantrāṇi; sarvatantrāṇi rūpam yasyāḥ sā sarvatantrarūpā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: sarva-tantra 'all the Tantras' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose form is all the Tantras'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition throughout.

components.meaning: Tantra, a body of scripture and practice (lit. 'loom, framework')

components.note: rūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose form is all the Tantras
names.significance: Names 204–206 together: She is the sound (mantra), the diagram (yantra) and the method (tantra) of Her own worship.

meaning_check.note: 'soul (embodiment)' replaced by the plain sense of the bahuvrīhi with rūpa 'form'.

sandhi.rule: a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā), inside unmanī

manas appears without its final s and its a coalesces with the u of unmanī by guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ). Regular sandhi of manaḥ + unmanī would leave a hiatus (mana unmanī); the fused form is that of the lexicalised technical term

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (traditional analysis), with an inner prādi-bahuvrīhi
samasa.vigraha: उद्गतम् मनः यस्याः सा उन्मनी; मनसः उन्मनी मनोन्मनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: udgatam manaḥ yasyāḥ sā unmanī; manasaḥ unmanī manonmanī
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: un-manī 'she whose mind has risen beyond', a bahuvrīhi with the prefix ut 'up, beyond' (manas is shortened and takes the feminine -ī): the state in which the mind is transcended. Outer layer: manas-unmanī 'the transcending of the mind', with manas in the genitive. The name is a technical term of Śaiva and Śākta yoga and is not built by ordinary sandhi.

components.note: appears as mano- in the name
manas, shortened, with feminine -ī in the bahuvrīhi unmanī

names.meaning: She who is Manonmanī, the state in which the mind transcends itself
names.significance: In Śaiva and Śākta yoga unmanī is the last stage of the subtle ascent of sound beyond the mind, where thought falls silent; Manonmanī is also the name of the highest of Śiva's nine powers in the Śaiva Āgamas.

meaning_check.note: 'Śiva's śakti' is one traditional identification but not what the name says; the name is the yogic state beyond the mind, and the identification is kept under significance.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is manas + unmanī ('the mind's going beyond').
names.uncertain: The junction mano + unmanī is not regular sandhi and the analysis of this technical term varies (some read manas + unmanī as a karmadhāraya, 'the mind that has become unmanī'); the meaning follows the common yogic sense.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the base maheśvara 'great lord'; the derivative then strengthens its first vowel (ma → mā, vṛddhi), a morphological change, not sandhi

components.meaning: belonging to Maheśvara; the consort and power of Maheśvara (Śiva)
components.note: taddhita (suffix -a with vṛddhi, feminine -ī) from maheśvara = mahā 'great' + īśvara 'lord'

names.meaning: She who is the consort of Maheśvara
names.significance: As the power (śakti) of the Great Lord She is inseparable from Him; Māheśvarī is also one of the seven Mothers (mātṛkās), the śakti of Maheśvara.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'maheshvara' put into IAST; 'consort' better gives the taddhita sense 'belonging to Maheśvara'.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; the name is the derivative of maheśvara (mahā + īśvara).

samasa.explanation: mahat 'great' qualifies devī 'goddess', the head; the feminine mahatī takes the masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva) and mahat becomes mahā- (Pāṇini 6.3.46). The name can also be read as the feminine of mahādeva, 'the consort of Mahādeva'. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
feminine of deva, from √div 'to shine, to play'

names.meaning: She who is the great Goddess
names.significance: Traditionally mahā is read as 'immeasurable': Her body cannot be measured, since it is the universe itself. She is also the consort of Mahādeva.

meaning_check.note: 'immeasurable body' is a commentarial gloss on mahā, not the meaning of the name; it is kept under significance.

samasa.explanation: mahat 'great' (as mahā-) qualifies lakṣmī, the head. Lakṣmī belongs to the small group of ī-stems that keep the nominative -s (-ḥ), unlike the derived feminines in -ī; hence mahālakṣmīḥ, which the verse shows as mahālakṣmīr before mṛḍa-.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: Lakṣmī, goddess of fortune and prosperity; fortune, splendor

names.meaning: She who is the great goddess Lakṣmī
names.significance: In the Devī Māhātmya Mahālakṣmī is the form of the Goddess who destroys Mahiṣa; here She is Lakṣmī not as one goddess among others but as the source of all fortune and splendor.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'lakShmI' put into IAST.

samasa.explanation: priyā 'beloved' is the head and Mṛḍa stands to it in the genitive: 'the beloved of Mṛḍa'. A bahuvrīhi reading (mṛḍaḥ priyaḥ yasyāḥ sā, 'She to whom Mṛḍa is dear') is also possible. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: Mṛḍa, 'the gracious one', a name of Śiva

names.meaning: She who is the beloved of Mṛḍa (Śiva)
names.significance: Mṛḍa names Śiva as gracious and kindly; She is dear to Him in His aspect of grace.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'mRiDa', 'shiva' put into IAST.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose form is great'; mahat appears as mahā- (Pāṇini 6.3.46) and rūpa takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who has a great form
names.significance: Traditionally Her form is great because it surpasses everything that has form, including the Purāṇic universe-form.

samasa.explanation: The gerundive pūjyā 'to be worshipped' is the head; mahā- 'greatly, supremely' qualifies it. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: to be worshipped, worthy of worship

names.meaning: She who is the greatest object of worship
names.significance: Traditionally even the gods who are themselves worshipped — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva — worship Her.

samasa.vigraha: महान्ति पातकानि महापातकानि; महापातकानाम् नाशिनी महापातकनाशिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahānti pātakāni mahāpātakāni; mahāpātakānām nāśinī mahāpātakanāśinī
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: mahā-pātaka 'great sins' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: nāśinī 'destroyer' (from the causative of √naś with the agent suffix -in) is the head and takes the sins in the genitive.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who destroys even the greatest of sins
names.significance: The mahāpātakas are the gravest sins of the Dharmaśāstra (such as killing a brāhmaṇa and theft of gold); traditionally even these are destroyed by remembrance of Her.

samasa.explanation: mahā- (from mahat) qualifies māyā, the head. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: māyā, the power that veils and projects; illusion

names.meaning: She who is the great illusion
names.significance: The Devī Māhātmya says that Mahāmāyā draws even the minds of the wise into delusion; the same power, when pleased, grants release.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose sattva is great'; sattva takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: sattva: being, essence; strength, courage; the guṇa of purity and light

names.meaning: She who possesses great sattva
names.significance: Sattva here covers both pure being and the strength or courage that flows from it; traditionally She is supreme in both.
names.previous_split_issues: sattvā was glossed 'being/essence' only; sattva also means strength, courage and the guṇa of purity.

samasa.explanation: mahā- qualifies śakti 'power', the head: 'the great Power'. Because śakti is itself feminine, a bahuvrīhi ('She whose power is great') would give the same form. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: power, energy; the Goddess as power

names.meaning: She who is the great Power
names.significance: She is not one power among many but the Power from which every other power is drawn.

meaning_check.note: As a karmadhāraya the name identifies Her with the great Power; 'has great power' is the weaker bahuvrīhi reading.

samasa.explanation: mahā- qualifies rati 'delight, love', the head. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: delight, joy, love; also Rati, consort of Kāma

names.meaning: She who is boundless delight
names.significance: Traditionally Her delight is the unending joy of the Self, of which every lesser pleasure is a faint reflection.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose enjoyment (or wealth) is great'; bhoga takes the feminine -ā. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who has immense wealth
names.significance: Bhoga is both enjoyment and the riches enjoyed; traditionally the whole universe is the object of Her enjoyment.

sandhi.rule: vṛddhi: ā + ai → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

samasa.explanation: 'She whose sovereignty is great'; aiśvarya takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
abstract noun from īśvara, with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who has supreme sovereignty
names.significance: Aiśvarya is the lordship of the Lord; traditionally Hers is the sovereignty that even the gods' powers derive from.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is mahā + aiśvaryā, fused by vṛddhi.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose valor is great'; vīrya takes the feminine -ā. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is supreme in valor
names.significance: Her valor is shown in the Purāṇic battles against Bhaṇḍa and the other demons; inwardly it is the strength that overcomes ignorance.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose strength is great'; bala takes the feminine -ā. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is supreme in might
names.significance: Traditionally Her might is that on which every other strength depends, as the Kena Upaniṣad shows the gods' powers failing without Brahman.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose intelligence is great'. Because buddhi is feminine, the bahuvrīhi keeps the form buddhiḥ. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is supreme in intelligence
names.significance: Traditionally She is the intelligence that illumines every intellect; Mahat or Buddhi is also the first evolute of nature, which She governs.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose attainments are great'; siddhi, being feminine, keeps its form. A karmadhāraya ('She who is the great attainment') is equally possible. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is endowed with the highest attainments
names.significance: The siddhis are the powers of the yogin, beginning with aṇimā; the greatest attainment is liberation, which She herself is.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: योगस्य ईश्वरः योगेश्वरः; महान्तः योगेश्वराः महायोगेश्वराः; महायोगेश्वराणाम् ईश्वरी महायोगेश्वरेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: yogasya īśvaraḥ yogeśvaraḥ; mahāntaḥ yogeśvarāḥ mahāyogeśvarāḥ; mahāyogeśvarāṇām īśvarī mahāyogeśvareśvarī
samasa.explanation: (1) yoga-īśvara 'lord of yoga', i.e. a master yogin (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mahā-yogeśvara 'the great lords of yoga' (karmadhāraya). (3) īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head of the whole and takes the great yogins in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the great lords of yoga'.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is the sovereign of the great lords of yoga
names.significance: Traditionally even the greatest yogins, Śiva foremost among them, are under Her rule and worship Her.

meaning_check.note: The name says She is the sovereign (īśvarī) of the great masters of yoga; 'object of worship' is an inference, not the grammar.

names.previous_split_issues: yogeśvareśvarī was left fused; it is yoga + īśvara + īśvarī, each junction by guṇa.

samasa.explanation: Formally a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose Tantra is great', with the feminine -ā; in sense it identifies Her with the great Tantra, as names 227 and 228 do with mantra and yantra. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: Tantra, scripture and system of practice

names.meaning: She who is the great Tantra
names.significance: Traditionally the great Tantras (the Kulārṇava, Jñānārṇava and others) are counted as Her body; She is both what they teach and the teaching itself.

meaning_check.note: 'Worshipped by the great Tantras' is not in the name; it describes Her as the great Tantra, parallel to names 227–228. The examples are kept under significance.

samasa.explanation: Formally 'She whose mantra is great', with the feminine -ā; in sense She is the great mantra itself. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is the greatest mantra
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the great mantra is Her fifteen-syllabled (pañcadaśī) vidyā, which is held to be Her sound-body.

samasa.explanation: Formally 'She whose yantra is great', with the feminine -ā; in sense She is the great yantra itself. No sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the great yantras
names.significance: The great yantra is the Śrīcakra, which in Śrīvidyā is not a symbol of Her but Her very form.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose seat is great'; āsana takes the feminine -ā. Mahā and āsanā fuse by savarṇa-dīrgha, so the name cannot be cut as mahā-sanā.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She whose seat is great
names.significance: Traditionally Her great seat is the whole hierarchy of the tattvas, or the couch formed by the five Brahmās (name 249).

meaning_check.note: āsana is singular in the compound and the bahuvrīhi says Her seat is great; 'seated on great seats' was loose.

names.previous_split_issues: The name was cut mahā-sanā and 'sanā' glossed 'seat'; the member is āsana 'seat', fused with mahā by savarṇa-dīrgha (mahā + āsanā).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: महान् यागः महायागः; महायागस्य क्रमः महायागक्रमः; महायागक्रमेण आराध्या महायागक्रमाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahān yāgaḥ mahāyāgaḥ; mahāyāgasya kramaḥ mahāyāgakramaḥ; mahāyāgakrameṇa ārādhyā mahāyāgakramārādhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) mahā-yāga 'the great sacrifice' (karmadhāraya). (2) mahāyāga-krama 'the ordered sequence of the great sacrifice' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head and takes the sequence in the instrumental: 'to be worshipped by the sequence of the great sacrifice'.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: to be worshipped, to be propitiated

names.meaning: She who is to be worshipped through the ordered rite of the great sacrifice
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the mahāyāga is the complete worship of the Śrīcakra, enclosure by enclosure in its prescribed order; inwardly it is the offering of all experience into the fire of consciousness.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'mahAyAga' put into IAST; krama 'ordered sequence' and the gerundive ārādhyā ('to be worshipped') were not rendered.

names.previous_split_issues: kramārādhyā was left fused; it is krama + ārādhyā.

samasa.vigraha: महान् भैरवः महाभैरवः; महाभैरवेण पूजिता महाभैरवपूजिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahān bhairavaḥ mahābhairavaḥ; mahābhairaveṇa pūjitā mahābhairavapūjitā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: mahā-bhairava 'the great Bhairava' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: the past participle pūjitā 'worshipped' is the head and takes the agent in the instrumental: 'worshipped by Mahābhairava'.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: Bhairava, the awe-inspiring form of Śiva
components.note: from bhīru 'fearful'; traditionally 'the one who bears, sustains and removes (the world)'

names.meaning: She who is worshipped even by Mahābhairava (Śiva)
names.significance: Traditionally Śiva as Mahābhairava, the Lord of dissolution, Himself worships Her.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'mahAbhairava', 'shiva' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside maheśvara 'great lord'

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhāraya, saptamī-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa layers)
samasa.vigraha: महान् ईश्वरः महेश्वरः; महान् कल्पः महाकल्पः; महत् ताण्डवम् महाताण्डवम्; महेश्वरस्य महाकल्पे महाताण्डवम् महेश्वरमहाकल्पमहाताण्डवम्; तस्य साक्षिणी महेश्वरमहाकल्पमहाताण्डवसाक्षिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahān īśvaraḥ maheśvaraḥ; mahān kalpaḥ mahākalpaḥ; mahat tāṇḍavam mahātāṇḍavam; maheśvarasya mahākalpe mahātāṇḍavam maheśvaramahākalpamahātāṇḍavam; tasya sākṣiṇī maheśvaramahākalpamahātāṇḍavasākṣiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) Three karmadhārayas: maheśvara 'the great Lord', mahā-kalpa 'the great aeon' (whose end is the great dissolution) and mahā-tāṇḍava 'the great dance'. (2) They combine as 'the great dance of Maheśvara at the great aeon('s end)', the Lord in the genitive and the aeon in the locative. (3) sākṣiṇī 'witness' is the head of the whole and takes the dance in the genitive: 'the witness of that dance'.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: aeon, cosmic age; the mahākalpa ends in the great dissolution
the tāṇḍava, Śiva's vigorous cosmic dance

names.meaning: She who is the witness of the great dance of Maheśvara (Śiva) at the end of the great cycle of creation
names.significance: When all else is dissolved at the end of the great aeon, Śiva dances and She alone remains to watch; traditionally this shows that She outlasts dissolution itself.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'maheshvara', 'shiva' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: कामस्य ईशः कामेशः; महान् कामेशः महाकामेशः; महाकामेशस्य महिषी महाकामेशमहिषी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmasya īśaḥ kāmeśaḥ; mahān kāmeśaḥ mahākāmeśaḥ; mahākāmeśasya mahiṣī mahākāmeśamahiṣī
samasa.explanation: (1) kāma-īśa 'the Lord of desire', Kāmeśvara (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mahā-kāmeśa 'the great Kāmeśa' (karmadhāraya). (3) mahiṣī 'chief queen' is the head and takes Him in the genitive.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is the great queen of Mahākāmeśvara (Śiva)
names.significance: Kāmeśvara is Śiva as Lord of desire, on whose lap She is seated (name 52, śiva-kāmeśvarāṅkasthā).

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'mahAkAmeshvara', 'shiva' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: kāmeśa was left fused (kāma + īśa).

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa and dvigu)
samasa.vigraha: त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुरे सुन्दरी त्रिपुरसुन्दरी; महती त्रिपुरसुन्दरी महात्रिपुरसुन्दरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripure sundarī tripurasundarī; mahatī tripurasundarī mahātripurasundarī
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-pura 'the three cities' (a dvigu of the collective type). (2) tripura-sundarī 'the beautiful one in the three cities', i.e. the most beautiful in all three worlds (saptamī-tatpuruṣa; a genitive reading is also given). (3) mahā- qualifies the whole: 'the great Tripurasundarī'.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

names.meaning: She who is the great Tripurasundarī, the beautiful one of the three cities
names.significance: Traditionally tripura is read through every triad — the three worlds, three bodies, three states, three guṇas, three syllable-groups of Her mantra — and She is the beauty that shines through all of them.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'tripurasundarI' put into IAST and the name explained.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of numeral and noun)
samasa.vigraha: चतुरधिका षष्टिः चतुःषष्टिः; चतुःषष्टिः उपचाराः चतुःषष्ट्युपचाराः; चतुःषष्ट्युपचारैः आढ्या चतुःषष्ट्युपचाराढ्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: caturadhikā ṣaṣṭiḥ catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ; catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ upacārāḥ catuḥṣaṣṭyupacārāḥ; catuḥṣaṣṭyupacāraiḥ āḍhyā catuḥṣaṣṭyupacārāḍhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) catuḥ-ṣaṣṭi 'sixty-four', i.e. 'sixty increased by four' (a karmadhāraya in which the middle word 'increased' is understood). (2) The numeral qualifies upacāra 'service of worship' (a dvigu-type karmadhāraya). (3) āḍhyā 'rich in, endowed with' is the head and takes the services in the instrumental: 'rich in the sixty-four services of worship'.

components.meaning: service, offering of worship (one of the attentions paid to the deity)

names.meaning: She who is honored with the sixty-four services of worship
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the fullest worship offers sixty-four upacāras, the services fit for a sovereign queen; inwardly they are the offering of every faculty to Her.

meaning_check.note: āḍhyā is 'rich in, endowed with'; upacāras are the services of worship, not 'ceremonies'.

names.previous_split_issues: catuṣ (assimilated form) was given for catur; upacārāḍhyā was left fused (upacāra + āḍhyā).

sandhi.rule: visarga: the final r of catur becomes visarga before a sibilant (Pāṇini 8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ), and the visarga may stay before ṣ (8.3.36 vā śari); the text keeps it rather than assimilating to catuṣṣaṣṭi

samasa.type: karmadhāraya of numeral and noun (over an inner karmadhāraya), followed by the taddhita suffix -maya
samasa.vigraha: चतुरधिका षष्टिः चतुःषष्टिः; चतुःषष्टिः कलाः चतुःषष्टिकलाः; चतुःषष्टिकलास्वरूपा चतुःषष्टिकलामयी
samasa.vigraha_iast: caturadhikā ṣaṣṭiḥ catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ; catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ kalāḥ catuḥṣaṣṭikalāḥ; catuḥṣaṣṭikalāsvarūpā catuḥṣaṣṭikalāmayī
samasa.explanation: (1) catuḥ-ṣaṣṭi 'sixty-four'. (2) catuḥṣaṣṭi-kalā 'the sixty-four arts' (numeral + noun). (3) The suffix -maya 'consisting of', feminine -mayī: 'consisting of the sixty-four arts'.

components.meaning: art, skill; also a digit or part

names.meaning: She who embodies the sixty-four fine arts
names.significance: The sixty-four arts range from music and painting to the crafts of daily life; traditionally the number also recalls the sixty-four Tantras which, the Saundaryalaharī (31) says, Śiva taught before Her own.
names.previous_split_issues: catuṣ (assimilated form) was given for catur.

sandhi.rule: visarga: the final r of catur becomes visarga before a sibilant (Pāṇini 8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ), and the visarga may stay before ṣ (8.3.36 vā śari); the text keeps it rather than assimilating to catuṣṣaṣṭi

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa layers)
samasa.vigraha: चतुःषष्टिः कोटयः चतुःषष्टिकोटयः; महत्यः चतुःषष्टिकोटयः योगिन्यः महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिन्यः; महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीनाम् गणाः महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीगणाः; तैः सेविता महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीगणसेविता
samasa.vigraha_iast: catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ koṭayaḥ catuḥṣaṣṭikoṭayaḥ; mahatyaḥ catuḥṣaṣṭikoṭayaḥ yoginyaḥ mahācatuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginyaḥ; mahācatuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginīnām gaṇāḥ mahācatuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginīgaṇāḥ; taiḥ sevitā mahācatuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginīgaṇasevitā
samasa.explanation: (1) catuḥṣaṣṭi-koṭi 'sixty-four crores' (numeral + noun). (2) mahā- 'great' and the number qualify yoginī, the yoginīs (karmadhāraya). (3) …yoginī-gaṇa 'the hosts of those yoginīs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The past participle sevitā 'served, attended' is the head and takes the hosts in the instrumental.

components.note: appears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

components.meaning: yoginī, a female attendant deity (also a female adept)

names.meaning: She who is served by the great hosts of sixty-four crore yoginīs
names.significance: Traditionally the yoginīs are attendant powers grouped under the Mothers (mātṛkās) of the Śrīcakra's enclosures; their countless number shows the reach of Her retinue.

meaning_check.note: Word order tidied: the number counts the yoginīs ('sixty-four crore yoginīs'), and 'yoginis' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: catuṣṣaṣṭi was given in the assimilated spelling; the text keeps the visarga (catuḥṣaṣṭi).
names.uncertain: Whether mahā- qualifies the number, the yoginīs or their hosts is not decided by the grammar; the sense hardly changes.

samasa.explanation: vidyā 'mantra-knowledge' is the head and Manu stands to it in the genitive: 'the vidyā of Manu', the form of the mantra that Manu worshipped. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: vidyā: knowledge; in Śrīvidyā, a mantra of the Goddess

names.meaning: She who is the Manuvidyā, the form of Her mantra worshipped by Manu
names.significance: Traditionally twelve great devotees — among them Manu, Candra, Kubera, Lopāmudrā, Agastya and Kāma — each worshipped Her through a form of the Śrīvidyā mantra; names 238 and 239 name two of them.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'manuvidyA' put into IAST and the term explained.

names.previous_split_issues: Manu was glossed 'progenitor' and vidyā 'knowledge'; in Śrīvidyā vidyā here means a mantra of the Goddess.

samasa.explanation: 'The vidyā of Candra (the Moon)', the form of Her mantra worshipped by the Moon. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: vidyā: in Śrīvidyā, a mantra of the Goddess

names.meaning: She who is the Candravidyā, the form of Her mantra worshipped by the Moon
names.significance: Another of the twelve traditional forms of the Śrīvidyā mantra, named after the devotee who worshipped Her through it.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'chandravidya' put into IAST and the term explained.

names.previous_split_issues: vidyā was glossed 'knowledge'; here it is a mantra of the Goddess.

samasa.vigraha: चन्द्रस्य मण्डलम् चन्द्रमण्डलम्; चन्द्रमण्डलस्य मध्यम् चन्द्रमण्डलमध्यम्; चन्द्रमण्डलमध्ये गच्छति तिष्ठति इति चन्द्रमण्डलमध्यगा
samasa.vigraha_iast: candrasya maṇḍalam candramaṇḍalam; candramaṇḍalasya madhyam candramaṇḍalamadhyam; candramaṇḍalamadhye gacchati tiṣṭhati iti candramaṇḍalamadhyagā
samasa.explanation: (1) candra-maṇḍala 'the disc of the moon' and (2) …maṇḍala-madhya 'its center' are ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas. (3) -gā 'going, being in' (from √gam) is the head and takes the center as its place: 'She who abides in the center of the moon's disc'.

components.note: √gam 'to go' + -a, feminine; only at the end of a compound

names.meaning: She who resides in the center of the moon's disc
names.significance: Traditionally the lunar disc is also inward: the cool, nectar-dropping moon in the thousand-petalled lotus at the crown of the head, where She is meditated upon.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'chandramaNDala' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: madhyagā was left fused; it is madhya 'center' + -gā 'abiding in'.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose form is beautiful'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

names.meaning: She whose form is beautiful
names.significance: Traditionally Her beauty, unlike the moon's of the previous names, neither waxes nor wanes.

meaning_check.note: 'A beauty that does not wax or wane' is a commentarial gloss drawn from the moon names; the name itself says 'beautiful form'. The gloss is kept under significance.

samasa.explanation: 'She whose smile is beautiful'; hāsa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

names.meaning: She who has a beautiful smile
names.significance: Traditionally Her smile is the visible sign of Her grace, and the devotee's sorrow dissolves before it.

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: चन्द्रस्य कला चन्द्रकला; चार्वी चन्द्रकला चारुचन्द्रकला; चारुचन्द्रकलाम् धरति इति चारुचन्द्रकलाधरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: candrasya kalā candrakalā; cārvī candrakalā cārucandrakalā; cārucandrakalām dharati iti cārucandrakalādharā
samasa.explanation: (1) candra-kalā 'a digit of the moon', the crescent (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) cāru 'lovely' qualifies it (karmadhāraya; the feminine cārvī takes the masculine stem cāru). (3) -dharā 'bearing, wearing' (√dhṛ + -a) is the head and governs the crescent as its object.

components.meaning: digit, a sixteenth part of the moon; crescent

names.meaning: She who wears a lovely crescent moon
names.significance: Traditionally the crescent on Her crown is the eternal digit that never waxes or wanes.

meaning_check.note: The old wording was garbled ('wears of beautiful crescent'); 'that does not wax or wane' is commentary and moved to significance.

names.previous_split_issues: kalādharā was left fused; it is kalā 'digit' + dharā 'bearing'.

a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and samāhāra-dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: चरम् च अचरम् च चराचरम्; चराचरम् जगत् चराचरजगत्; चराचरजगतः नाथा चराचरजगन्नाथा
samasa.vigraha_iast: caram ca acaram ca carācaram; carācaram jagat carācarajagat; carācarajagataḥ nāthā carācarajagannāthā
samasa.explanation: (1) cara-acara 'the moving and the unmoving' (dvandva; carācara is also explained as a reduplicated adjective from √car). (2) It qualifies jagat 'world' (karmadhāraya). (3) nāthā 'mistress, ruler', the feminine of nātha, is the head and takes the world in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the ruler of the animate and inanimate worlds
names.significance: Nātha is a protector as well as a ruler; traditionally She guards every being, moving or still, as Her own.
names.previous_split_issues: carācara and jagannāthā were left fused; they are cara + acara and jagat + nāthā.

samasa.vigraha: चक्राणाम् राजा चक्रराजः; चक्रराजः निकेतनम् यस्याः सा चक्रराजनिकेतना
samasa.vigraha_iast: cakrāṇām rājā cakrarājaḥ; cakrarājaḥ niketanam yasyāḥ sā cakrarājaniketanā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: cakra-rāja 'the king of cakras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; rājan becomes rāja at the end of a tatpuruṣa, Pāṇini 5.4.91 rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣ ṭac). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose abode is the king of cakras'; niketana takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She whose abode is the king of cakras, the Śrīcakra
names.significance: The Śrīcakra is called the king of cakras; She dwells in it as in Her own palace, and in Śrīvidyā it is identical with Her body and with the body of the worshipper.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'shrI chakra' put into IAST (Śrīcakra) and 'king of cakras' rendered.

names.previous_split_issues: rāja was glossed 'king/royal' as if an independent adjective; it is rājan 'king' as head of cakra-rāja.

components.note: taddhita from parvata 'mountain' (vṛddhi of the first syllable, feminine -ī)

names.meaning: She who is the daughter of the Mountain (Himavat)
names.significance: As Pārvatī, daughter of Himavat, the supreme Goddess enters the Purāṇic story as the consort whom Śiva wins and who wins Śiva by austerity.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'HimAlaya' put into IAST; 'Mount Himavat or Himālaya' simplified to Himavat.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; the name is one derived word (taddhita from parvata).

samasa.vigraha: पद्मे इव नयने यस्याः सा पद्मनयना
samasa.vigraha_iast: padme iva nayane yasyāḥ sā padmanayanā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose eyes are like lotuses': padma is the standard of comparison for nayana, and the whole is a bahuvrīhi; nayana takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

names.meaning: She whose eyes are like lotuses
names.significance: Lotus eyes are long, soft and wide open; traditionally they are also eyes that look on all with compassion.

meaning_check.note: 'Long and beautiful like the petals' is an elaboration; the name compares the eyes to lotuses.

names.previous_split_issues: nayanā was glossed 'eyed'; the member is nayana 'eye', given the feminine ending of the bahuvrīhi.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi and tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: पद्मस्य इव रागः यस्य सः पद्मरागः; पद्मरागेण समा पद्मरागसमा; पद्मरागसमा प्रभा यस्याः सा पद्मरागसमप्रभा
samasa.vigraha_iast: padmasya iva rāgaḥ yasya saḥ padmarāgaḥ; padmarāgeṇa samā padmarāgasamā; padmarāgasamā prabhā yasyāḥ sā padmarāgasamaprabhā
samasa.explanation: (1) padma-rāga 'lotus-hued', the ruby (a bahuvrīhi that has become a noun). (2) padmarāga-samā 'equal to the ruby' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: words of equality govern the instrumental). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose radiance is equal to that of the ruby'; sama takes the masculine stem before prabhā (puṃvadbhāva).

components.meaning: ruby (lit. 'having the color of the lotus')

names.meaning: She whose radiance equals that of the ruby
names.significance: The ruby-red continues the crimson of Her form (names 6 and 12); in Śrīvidyā the red is the color of compassion and of vimarśa, Her self-awareness.

meaning_check.note: Literal sense restored: Her radiance equals the ruby's; 'resplendent red complexion' was a paraphrase.

names.previous_split_issues: rāga was glossed 'passion/love/desire'; in padmarāga 'ruby' it means 'color'. samaprabhā was left fused.

verse_notes.note: Name 194: durācāra is the prefix dus (dur) + ācāra 'conduct'. Name 198 echoes the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (6.8): none is equal to Her, none greater.
Names 199–206 form a run of sarva- ('all') names: She is all powers, all auspiciousness, all mantras, yantras and Tantras.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga becomes r before a voiced sound

verse_notes.note: Name 210 ends in -ḥ (mahālakṣmīḥ): lakṣmī keeps the nominative s, which surfaces as r before mṛḍa-. Name 208 begins the long run of mahā- names that continues to name 237.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga becomes r before a voiced sound

verse_notes.note: Name 220 is mahā + aiśvaryā fused by vṛddhi (mahaiśvaryā); name 225 is one name, the sovereign of the great lords of yoga.
Name 229 is mahā + āsanā (mahāsanā, 'whose seat is great'), not mahā-sanā.
Name 232 fills the whole first half: Maheśvara's great dance at the end of the great aeon, and She its witness.
Names 235–237 spell 'sixty-four' with the visarga kept (catuḥṣaṣṭi, Pāṇini 8.3.36 vā śari); catuṣṣaṣṭi is the equally correct assimilated spelling.
Names 238–239 are two of the traditional twelve forms of the Śrīvidyā mantra, named after their worshippers (Manu, the Moon); names 239–243 gather round the moon.
Name 248: padmarāga 'lotus-hued' is the ruby; rāga here means color, not passion.

report.summary: Checked all 56 names of ślokas 51–60 (names 193–248) against text.json: sandhi at every member junction, a layered samāsa analysis with vigraha-vākyas in pausa form, and the meanings against that analysis. One reading form was wrongly cut (229: mahāsanā is mahā + āsanā, not mahā-sanā), and several meanings carried commentary in place of the grammar (207, 209, 225, 226, 241) or misread a suffix (203 -mayī 'consisting of', not 'pervading'); these were replaced. External sandhi joins names only by visarga → r in ślokas 53–55. No problem was found in the Sanskrit text.
